correctness.rationale: A section vertex is either an original vertex in the hyperplane or a strict crossing of an original edge, by taking the minimal containing face. At a vertex-avoiding level, the opposite-sign count is s(2d−s), and the missing antipodal edges among these number min(s,2d−s) because the two values in an antipodal pair have the same sum at that level. Nested positive sets on the two levels give k−ell vertical crossings. All layer-count pairs occur: fix a base direction with distinct nonzero absolute coordinates and select each of the two parallel thresholds in the gap producing the desired count, including exterior gaps; ordered thresholds are equivalent to a nonnegative vertical normal, and equal thresholds are allowed. The two separated quadratic pieces have unique integer maximizers k=d+1 and ell=d−1, yielding exactly 2d(d−1)+2. For a hyperplane containing vertices, choose a nonempty strict side. Each vertex in the hyperplane has an incident edge into that side: the tangent cone is generated by edge directions and contains a direction to a point in the side. A sufficiently small parallel shift keeps all strict crossings and adds one distinct crossing per previously contained vertex. This includes the supporting case. For the unrestricted cut, an unbalanced base split has at most d²−1 complete-graph crossings, while any balanced split for odd d cuts at least one deleted antipodal edge. Complementary maximizing balanced splits add all vertical edges. These facts give the stated abstract cut deficit. Independent exact replay used a fixed-direction gap construction in d=2–10 and examined 15,708 nongeneric integer cases, but the dimension-independent proof supplies the bounds.
residual_risks: The displayed spectrum is generic only; the sharp maximum applies to all sections. No nongeneric spectrum or f-vector result claimed.
